subtopics.title: Themes and how to study the passages

outcomes.text: Explore the major theme(s) in each set passage: God in himself, God's relationship with the created world, God's Messengers.
Explain why these themes matter in the lives of Muslims today.
Study the passages in English translation with reference to the original Arabic, and know both.
Sura 2.255 (Ayat al-Kursi): God is living, eternal, all-knowing and supreme; no one intercedes without permission.
Sura 6.101-103: God is Creator of everything, has no son, and cannot be grasped by sight.
Sura 41.37: Sun and moon are signs of God, not to be worshipped; worship their Creator.
Sura 42.4-5: Everything belongs to God, the angels praise him, and he is forgiving and merciful.
Sura 112 (al-Ikhlas): God is one, eternal, neither begets nor is begotten, and has no equal.

subtopics.title: God's relationship with the created world (set passages)

outcomes.text: Sura 1 (al-Fatiha): praise of God as sustainer, merciful, master of the Day of Judgement, and a prayer for guidance.
Sura 2.21-22: People should worship their Creator who made the earth a resting place and the sky a canopy.
Sura 96.1-5: The first revelation: read in the name of the Lord who created and taught humans.
Sura 99 (al-Zalzala): The earth's shaking on the last day and every deed, small or great, being shown.
Sura 114 (al-Nas): Seeking refuge in God from the whisperings of evil.
Sura 2.30-37: God makes humans vicegerents on earth; the story of Adam, the angels and the fall.
Sura 6.75-79: Ibrahim reasons from the stars, moon and sun to belief in the one God.
Sura 5.110: God's favours to Isa, his miracles and the people's response.
Sura 93 (al-Duha): God has not forsaken Muhammad and will give him more; care for orphans and the needy.
Sura 108 (al-Kawthar): God's abundance to Muhammad, prayer and sacrifice, and the fate of his enemy.

topics.title: 2. The history and importance of the Qur'an

subtopics.title: The Qur'an: revelation, compilation and role

outcomes.text: Describe the revelation of the Qur'an to the Prophet between 610 and 632.
Give the account of the compilation of the Qur'an under the Rightly Guided Caliphs.
Know the major themes of the Qur'an in the set passages and in similar passages.
Explain the Qur'an's use in legal thinking and its relationship with Hadith, consensus (ijma') and analogy (qiyas).
Explain its significance as the basis of all thought and action in Islam.

topics.title: 3. The life and importance of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

outcomes.text: Recount the main events of the Prophet's life from birth to his call to prophethood.
Recount the main events of his activities in Makka and his experiences with opponents.
Recount the main events of his time in Madina, his leadership there, and conflicts with the Makkans and others.
Describe his actions and character.

subtopics.title: Importance of the Prophet as an example

outcomes.text: Explain the importance of his actions as examples for individuals' conduct and relations with others, including women and non-Muslims.
Explain the importance of his actions as examples for Muslim communities in relations with other states.
Explain his significance as Seal of the Prophets and last Messenger of God.
Know the Prophet's wives and the significant facts of their lives.
Know his descendants: children, grandchildren, and the line recognised as Imams by Shi'a Muslims.
Know his leading Companions, including the Ten Blessed Companions, his scribes, the Emigrants and Helpers, and the four Rightly Guided Caliphs during his lifetime.
Explain the importance of these people's actions and experiences in Islamic history and belief.

topics.title: 1. Major teachings in the Hadiths of the Prophet

subtopics.title: Themes and how to study the passages

outcomes.text: Study the Hadith passages on individual conduct and life in the community.
Draw out what each passage teaches Muslims about belief and action.
Study the passages with reference to the Arabic as well as the English.

subtopics.title: Hadiths on individual conduct and faith

outcomes.text: Religion is sincerity: to God, his Book, his Messenger, Muslim leaders and the common people.
Believers should want for their brother what they want for themselves.
Believers speak good or stay silent, and are generous to neighbours and guests.
Fulfilling obligations and respecting lawful and forbidden things leads to paradise.
Every good act, such as justice, a kind word or clearing the road, is a charity.
Change evil by hand, tongue or heart, the last being the weakest faith.
Modesty brings only good; faith the size of a mustard seed versus pride.
God looks at hearts and deeds, not forms and possessions.
The world is the believer's prison and the unbeliever's paradise.
The best of people is the believer who strives hard in God's way with person and property.
Martyrdom has wider forms than death in battle, such as plague and natural death in God's way.
The best food is earned by one's own hands.
Caring for widows, the poor and orphans is like striving in God's way.
Leaders should be gentle and bring cheer, as in the instruction to Abu Musa and Mu'adh.
Studying the Qur'an is like tending tethered camels: it must be kept up.
Be kindly when buying, selling and asking for debts back.
God does not show mercy to those who show none to others.
Believers are like one body, each feeling the pain of another.

topics.title: 2. The history and importance of the Hadiths

outcomes.text: Describe the history of the compilation of the Hadiths and the earliest collections.
Know the main musnad and musannaf collections and the main compilers and their work.
Explain the isnad and matn methods for testing the reliability of a Hadith.
Describe the main features of the six Sunni and four Shi'a Hadith collections.
Know the major themes of Hadith in the set and similar passages.
Explain the use of Hadith in legal thinking and its relationship with the Qur'an, ijma' and qiyas.
Explain the significance of Hadith in thought and action in Islam.

topics.title: 3. The period of rule of the Rightly Guided Caliphs and their importance as leaders

outcomes.text: Recount the main events of the rules of the four Caliphs.
Describe their policies in maintaining and expanding the state.
Describe their approaches to leading the community.
Describe their main achievements and the main difficulties they met.
Explain their significance as examples of leadership.
Explain the importance of their rules as models for government today.
Explain their importance as examples for Muslim communities' relations with other states.

topics.title: 4. The Articles of Faith and the Pillars of Islam

outcomes.text: God: what Muslims believe about him.
Angels: their nature and duties.
Books: their contents and purpose.
Prophets: their character and function.
God's predestination and decree: meaning and significance.
Resurrection and the last day: the main events and significance.
Explain jihad in its range of meanings: physical, mental and spiritual.
Shahada: the declaration of faith and the significance of what it contains.
Salat: preparations, performance, importance, Friday and festival congregations, times, place, private and delayed prayer.
Zakat: how alms-giving is performed and its significance in the community.
Sawm: how fasting is observed, its significance and who is exempt.
Hajj: the main observances of pilgrimage and their significance.
Explain the significance of each belief and observance for individuals and communities.
